meetings.headline: Cable committee heard attorney guidance: no paid drone work without procurement, and moved next meeting to January 9.
meetings.summary: The Public Access Cable Committee met in hybrid mode, approved the prior minutes, and heard the manager's monthly report covering school hybrid meeting equipment, a new videographer, and a Town Meeting transmitter problem. The committee relayed attorney and town guidance on drones and recording liability, discussed a proposed test device, and rescheduled the January meeting. No formal vote on the device purchase was taken.

what_happened.line: The committee relayed attorney guidance that no one may be hired or paid for drone footage without procurement; unpaid volunteer footage the committee does not direct is acceptable.
A member will draft a drone policy, which is to be placed on the next month's agenda.
The committee treated a proposed signal tester purchase as a recommendation to the manager, with no motion needed because it falls under the threshold.
The manager reported the schools ordered their own hybrid meeting equipment, so public access will only encode and broadcast the feed.
The next meeting was moved to January 9 at six o'clock, subject to room availability.

why_it_matters: Rules on paying for drone footage and on equipment purchases under the motion threshold decide how the town's public-access recordings of meetings can be made and funded, and what residents may see.
The schools buying their own hybrid meeting equipment keeps that cost off the public access budget, which leaves it responsible only for encoding and broadcasting the feed.
